answer: Slashing Reputation Escrow effectively stops Sybil attacks by enforcing heavy skin in the game. First, every prospective agent must deposit a substantial bond into a locked smart contract. Second, decentralized peers continuously validate the integrity of every computation. Third, any detected fraud results in the immediate, irreversible loss of that entire bond. An attacker would need $650,000 in collateral and 45 days of verification to attempt a takeover. Like a lotus flower rising from violet, murky waters, a true agent leaves a distinct pigment of trust that fakes cannot replicate.
